Equivalence is not yet established, because no run is cited.", "artifacts": [{"kind": "equivalence_report", "title": "Equivalence report: gray_counter.v (gold) vs gray_counter_refactor.v (gate)", "summary": "This report serves [requirement:req-5de0de52be]. It compares two approved versions of module gray_counter. The gold version is [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a1] gray_counter.v (sha256:7e2c53ab…). The gate version is [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a2] gray_counter_refactor.v (sha256:96d802d2…). Both have the same module name and the same ports: clk, rst, en, gray[3:0], wrap. Each has one state register, gray[3:0], with a synchronous reset to 4'b0000. The compare points are the outputs gray[3:0] and wrap, plus the state register gray, which matches by name. Every compare point should therefore map, and none is expected to be left unmapped. The setup file gray_counter_equiv.eqy reads each version on its own and elaborates top gray_counter. It then runs the eqy sby strategy with engine smtbmc. My manual reading found matching next-state logic and matching wrap logic. Gold computes the next code by decoding to binary, adding one and re-encoding. Gate flips bit 0 when parity is even. When parity is odd, gate flips the bit above the lowest set bit, or bit 3 for 1000, which wraps to 0000. For wrap, gold's en && gray==1000 is the same function as gate's en & gray[3] & ~|gray[2:0]. This reading is only a claim and proves nothing. The verdict waits for the platform's equivalence.run result on this setup. === FILE: gray_counter_equiv.eqy ===
[gold]
read_verilog gray_counter.v
prep -top gray_counter

[gate]
read_verilog gray_counter_refactor.v
prep -top gray_counter

[strategy sby]
use sby
depth 10
engine smtbmc
=== END FILE ===
